London, 22<sup>nd</sup> January 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Tanaka Kikinzoku Kogyo** said on Wednesday it handled a record volume of platinum in 2008, with investor interest growing strongly at a time when other financial markets plunged. Tanaka Kikinzoku Kogyo’s platinum sales volume surged to a record high in October, and sales -- or purchases by investors -- stayed near that level in November and December, an official at the company said. 

Tanaka’s sales of platinum have exceeded its purchases, or investors unloading the metal at the company, since July, and sales were nearly three-fold those of purchases in 2008.  Tanaka sold 2.7 times more platinum than it bought in 2008, and it was up 526 percent from 2007. Tanaka’s purchases of platinum also rose 149 percent from 2007.Market conditions have also been favourable for the company as falling prices boosted the appeal for investors.  The price of platinum rose to 7,589 yen per gram in March, the highest since Tanaka Kikinzoku began sales of the precious metal in 1976, but fell to 2,454 yen in November, the lowest since 2003. 

## _Source:  Reuters Africa_ 

**The French government** yesterday offered the country’s carmakers up to €6bn (£5.5bn) in aid after Carlos Ghosn, Renault’s chief executive, warned that without rapid state intervention, Europe’s entire auto industry faced collapse. 

## _Source:  Guardian_ 

**General Motors** said yesterday  it received a delayed payment of $5.4 billion under the emergency funding provided by the U.S. government to keep it in business.  GM COO Fritz Henderson said late on Tuesday that the automaker would have run out of cash and faced bankruptcy if it had not been given the second loan tranche from the U.S. government.  The loan payout was the second in a total of $13.4 billion pledged to GM by the U.S. Treasury.  GM has now received $9.4 billion of that amount and expects to get a final $4 billion payment on Feb. 17 when it faces a deadline to submit a restructuring plan to Congress. GM posted its global sales for 2008 earlier on Wednesday showing that it finished behind rival Toyota Motor Corp for the first time in 77 years. 

## _Source:   Automotive News_ 

**An estimated 17 000 mineworkers** marched to the Rustenburg offices of Anglo Platinum’s Rustenburg operations on Wednesday afternoon, to demand an investigation into the disappearance of two workers.  The National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) is demanding an independent investigation into the disappearance of two of its members in 1991, and 2002 respectively.  NUM spokesman Linzwi Kwezi said that both miners had gone underground at the Frank shaft, and had never been heard from again. Angloplat spokesperson Simon Tebele said that production would not be affected by the march.  Tebele added that, directly after the disappearance of the two mineworkers, investigations were launched by members of the police, the Department of Minerals and Energy, members of management, as well as

union representatives. However, the investigations were called off owing to a lack of information. Tebele stated that the investigations would only be restarted once new information was received.   Kwezi claimed that the initial investigations had only concentrated on the surface, and had never gone underground. NUM was also demanding that a mineworker, who the union claimed died at the mine and was buried by management at the scene, be exhumed. 

## _Source:  Mining Weekly_
